# Mercury Agent

> Mercury is an open-source, soul-driven AI agent that runs on your own machine. It reaches you from the terminal, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal and a local web dashboard, keeps a local long-term memory, asks before it acts through a permission system, stays inside a daily token budget, and keeps running as a background service. It ships Mercury Code (a coding environment) and Mercury Bots (persistent specialist agents).

Desktop app: Mercury Desktop for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux at https://mercuryagent.sh/download. It installs Mercury on the computer or connects to one elsewhere, and keeps both updated.

Install: `curl -fsSL https://mercuryagent.sh/install.sh | sh` (macOS/Linux), `irm https://mercuryagent.sh/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows), or `npm i -g @cosmicstack/mercury-agent` on Node.js 22+. Source: https://github.com/cosmicstack-labs/mercury-agent (MIT).

## Docs

- [Getting started](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs): install, first run, channels
- [Mercury Desktop](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/desktop/mercury-desktop): install the app, first run, connecting to a remote Mercury
- [Updating Mercury](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/desktop/updating): desktop and server updates, rollback, required updates
- [Remote access & security](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/desktop/remote-access): owner approvals, device tokens, /server
- [CLI commands](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/cli-commands/cli-commands): every `mercury` command
- [Permissions model](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/reference/permissions): scopes, approvals, blocklist
- [Second Brain memory](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/reference/second-brain): how memory is extracted and recalled
- [Mercury Code](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/integrations/coding-workspace): the coding environment
- [Mercury Bots](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/integrations/mercury-bots): persistent bots and fleets
- [Release notes](https://mercuryagent.sh/docs/releases)

## Blog

- [Mercury Weekly #1: IPOs, models and agents that pay](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/mercury-weekly-1.md) (2026-11-17): The week of 9 to 15 November 2026: Anthropic's IPO roadshow, Nvidia's CEO change, new frontier models, ChatGPT Wallet and the Decisions API.
- [What Is a Personal AI Assistant? 10 Real Tasks in 2026](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/what-is-a-personal-ai-assistant.md) (2026-11-11): A personal AI assistant acts for one person across accounts, files, apps and services. What it is, ten tasks it handles, and the permissions each needs.
- [9 AI Agents Compared for Real Work: Memory and Permissions](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/six-ai-agents-compared-for-real-work.md) (2026-11-05): Nine AI agents compared on memory, where they run, what they can touch, scheduling, permissions, model choice and price.
- [Mercury 1.5: Mercury Desktop](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/mercury-1-5.md) (2026-11-03): Mercury 1.5.0 ships Mercury Desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux, remote access the owner approves, and updates that roll back on their own.
- [A tour of Mercury Desktop: one app, every Mercury you run](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/mercury-desktop-tour.md) (2026-11-03): What's inside Mercury Desktop 1.5.0: chat, research, code, bots, memory and voice, plus connecting to several Mercury servers and keeping them all updated.
- [Your agent returned 200 OK. It may still have failed](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/agent-observability-first-wrong-step.md) (2026-10-31): What to record in an AI agent run to find its first wrong step, and what Mercury records today. Based on OpenTelemetry's GenAI agent spans and a code review.
- [Running an agent overnight: what breaks first](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/running-an-agent-overnight.md) (2026-10-27): We read Mercury's scheduler and budget code and reproduced one behaviour to find what fails in long unattended runs: skipped tasks and quiet errors.
- [How Optimus works: an agent that uses your computer](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/how-optimus-works.md) (2026-10-24): Inside Optimus, the Mercury plugin that sees your screen, moves the mouse and types: its processes, how it looks and acts, voice control, and the safety rails.
- [Mercury 1.4: plugins, WhatsApp calls, and Optimus](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/mercury-1-4.md) (2026-10-23): Mercury 1.4 adds isolated plugins, WhatsApp chat with voice calls both ways, and Optimus, which sees your screen and uses your mouse.
- [AI coding's bottleneck is verification, not generation](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/ai-coding-verification-bottleneck.md) (2026-10-20): A Harvard working paper finds coding agents raised output while review time rose 49%. Why verification should decide whether an agent is useful.
- [Agents exceeded their permissions: how to scope them](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/agent-permissions-least-privilege.md) (2026-10-17): CERT-In says AI agents read live business records at Indian firms. Here is how least privilege, scoped access, approvals and audit logs should limit them.
- [Mercury Bots: an agent fleet that runs on your machine](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/mercury-bots.md) (2026-10-16): How Mercury Bots work, what we measured, how they compare with other always-on agents, and the commits behind them, as the work was done.
- [The setup wizard that quit at the first menu](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/the-wizard-that-quit-at-the-menu.md) (2026-10-15): A new Mercury install asked for your name, showed one menu, then quit with no error. How a one-tick race caused it, and the test that stops it returning.
- [We were running Mercury twice and didn't know it](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/we-were-running-mercury-twice.md) (2026-10-14): Typing felt sluggish everywhere. The cause was a second full copy of the agent, started quietly by the launcher. How we found it and fixed it.
- [Mercury 1.3: an agent you can actually leave running](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/mercury-1-3.md) (2026-10-12): Mercury 1.3's shared background runtime, bots that deliver real files and stay online, and a fleet you run from Telegram. What changed and why.
- [Asks before it acts: how Mercury's permission model works](https://mercuryagent.sh/blog/asks-before-it-acts.md) (2026-10-09): How Mercury's permission model works: scopes, approvals, a blocklist nothing overrides, an SSRF guard, and the limits that apply to unattended bots.
